title: TikTok Owes $400 Million for Breaking Kids' Privacy Rules
summary:
Imagine a giant piggy bank with $400 million inside. That's how much TikTok has to pay the U.S. government for breaking rules about kids' privacy. The government said TikTok collected personal information from kids under 13 without asking their parents first. That's against a law called COPPA, which protects children online.

The U.S. Department of Justice said TikTok will pay $300 million right away and another $100 million later. A man named Stanley Woodward Jr., who works for the government, said, "This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents." He wants companies to keep kids safe online.

TikTok also didn't delete accounts when parents asked them to, even when they knew the accounts belonged to young kids. That made the government upset.

TikTok has been changing a lot. In January, it made a deal with big companies like Oracle and Silver Lake to create a new TikTok U.S. company. This might help them follow the rules better.

Other social media apps are also in trouble. Instagram's parent company, Meta, is in court right now for similar problems. Many countries are making rules to keep kids off social media or protect their privacy.

So, next time you use an app, remember: companies are supposed to keep your information safe, especially if you're under 13. And if they don't, they might have to pay a LOT of money.
why_it_matters: This matters because you may use apps like TikTok, and rules like COPPA are meant to stop companies from taking your personal information without your family's permission.

background_read: The U.S. Department of Justice (the part of the U.S. government that enforces federal laws) said TikTok must pay this settlement.
COPPA is a U.S. law that requires apps and websites to get a parent's permission before collecting personal information from children under 13.
Meta (the parent company of Instagram and Facebook) is facing similar legal trouble over how it handles young users' data.
